name: feral-special-clemence-attempt-01b
prompt:
Create an ORIGINAL native RGBA sprite sheet as a new drawing of Feral Predator, NOT a rig or mirror. LANDSCAPE composition 1536 wide by 1024 high. EXACTLY TWO COLUMNS and FOUR ROWS, eight separate full-figure cells, each cell 768x256. All figures on this page face LEFT, back/left three-quarter view. The other facing will be independently drawn on another page. VERY SMALL FIGURES: standing body from mask crown to feet about 150 pixels and NEVER taller than 180 pixels; this deliberately leaves transparent space. With mannequin, both standing bodies must use that same150px body height, combined scene width under550px. A full transparent gutter at least40px must surround EVERY scene. Do not use all available cell height. No figure, hand, spear tip, foot or prop may enter neighboring cells. Native alpha: every pixel outside each separate scene exactly alpha0. NO cast shadow, NO ground plane, NO glow, NO gradient, NO smoke, NO text, NO visible grid. Opaque well-lit detailed body, but illumination NEVER painted into empty transparent pixels.
Identity matches inspected references exactly: lean sinewy ochre spotted skin, black dreadlocks, ivory bone skull mask with exposed red mandibles, dark segmented loincloth, asymmetrical bone ornaments, bronze bracers, ankle wraps/clawed feet; no shoulder cannon. Gear anatomically consistent: shield on LEFT forearm, right wrist bracer as source. Nonlethal source mercy choreography study with a neutral articulated gray training mannequin/partner stand-in. Feral holds one whole spear. The stand-in has one simple training blade; one small sealed mission case lies nearby. No injury, blood, execution or anatomical trophy. This is a scene study, not a combat sprite with a duplicated real opponent.
Read cells left to right then top to bottom, not a comic panel. Cell1 is body-scale calibration ONLY: Feral alone in neutral full-body guard with spear lowered, bracer blades retracted and left shield folded. Cell1 is outside animation; no mannequin or spare props in calibration. Seven completely new independently articulated source choreography stages occupy cells2 through8:
Cell2: Feral hooks the neutral gray stand-in's training blade with his spear and twists it away from the grip; both complete bodies fit in the cell.
Cell3: The training blade visibly drops to the ground as Feral controls his spear and steps his rear foot backward, leaving the stand-in unharmed.
Cell4: Feral has moved a full step back with lowered weapon and open free palm, giving the neutral stand-in clear space to recover its stance.
Cell5: Feral bends to collect the same small sealed mission case from the ground with his free LEFT hand, spear held down in the RIGHT; stand-in stays unharmed at a distance.
Cell6: He straightens holding the sealed case and the lowered spear, looking once toward the stand-in rather than taking an anatomical trophy.
Cell7: He turns his torso slightly to leave with that case, spear safely lowered and an open space between him and the upright recovering stand-in.
Cell8: Feral takes one small walking departure step with the same sealed mission case in his left hand and spear lowered in the right; the unhurt stand-in remains upright behind him.
Every mannequin is an obviously gray articulated training dummy, no human face, blood, gore, injuries, trophy or terror. Whole body effort, contact, controlled withdrawal and recovery must be distinct. This is a SCENE CHOREOGRAPHY VISUAL STUDY; synchronization with a separate actual opponent is not claimed. Keep exact same props through the sequence. Do not leave duplicate weapons where Feral already collected them. Do not replace a finishing sequence with seven victory poses. Draw all cells newly, not repeated neutral silhouettes.
DIRECTION IS MANDATORY: every mask nose points toward the LEFT EDGE of the canvas, as in the one supplied LEFT reference. Feral is on the RIGHT HALF of EACH action cell. The training mannequin and any training blade are on the LEFT HALF of that cell. Feral's front foot points LEFT. Spear actions/parry/contact reach LEFT. Do NOT draw the action rightward; rear three-quarter view is NOT enough without LEFTWARD nose and LEFTWARD target. The independently drawn left figure is not a horizontal reflection of right art.
The entire scene is like a TINY MINIATURE in the CENTER HALF of each cell, not a body filling the frame. Leave at least a full quarter-cell blank above and below each scene, even crouches. Retract right wrist blades entirely inside the bracer in every drawing; no protruding silver tips at all.
